tasks.author: ai-task-writer-f
tasks.prompt: Summarise what a script runner must and should do when it reads a script's embedded dependencies and Python requirement, including edge cases.

rubric.text: It must error if the declared dependencies cannot be provided.
It should (not must) error if no Python version satisfying requires-python can be provided.
If it manages Python versions, it should try the highest available version compatible with requires-python.
For a script fetched from a URL, it must not install dependencies until the user has seen the declared dependencies.
Unclosed blocks are ignored, and multiple blocks of the same type are an error.

tasks.author: ai-task-writer-f
tasks.prompt: Explain the rules an automated tool must follow when it adds a dependency to a script's embedded metadata.

rubric.text: Add to the existing script block rather than starting a second block of the same type, which would be an error.
Keep the closing # /// line and keep every line of the block a comment (a # followed by a space, or a bare #).
Do not move the dependencies into a separate requirements file.
Each added entry must be a valid PEP 508 dependency.
Preserving TOML formatting is nice to have, not required.

tasks.notes: Cross-section: Notes for automated tools, Specification, Reference Implementation.
